title: Vivas v. Monetary Board of BSP
respondent: Monetary Board of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
summary: The Supreme Court upheld the power of the Monetary Board to close and place a bank under receivership without prior notice and hearing. The close-now-hear-later doctrine applies to bank closures to protect depositors and the banking system.
doctrine: The Monetary Board may order the closure of a bank and place it under receivership without prior notice and hearing (close-now-hear-later doctrine). This is not a violation of due process because the bank has the remedy of filing a petition for certiorari to question the closure. The urgency of bank closures justifies summary action.
fullText:
BRION, J.:

The issue is whether the Monetary Board's order closing the petitioner bank and placing it under receivership without prior notice and hearing violates due process.

Section 30 of RA 7653 authorizes the Monetary Board to close a banking institution upon finding that it is unable to pay its liabilities as they become due, or that its continuance in business would involve probable loss to its depositors or creditors.

The close-now-hear-later doctrine has been upheld by the Court. The summary closure of a bank is justified by the urgent need to protect depositors and the stability of the banking system. The affected bank may question the closure through appropriate judicial proceedings.
